problem: 'Kusetyenziswe kule nyanga' = 'used this month' without saying money; next to rand figure and beside 'Kuvunwe' it can read as produce used. English 'Spent' = money out.
'Izithole' means heifers (young cows) in isiXhosa, not seedlings. The placeholder would show farmers an example about livestock in a seed/cost field. Seedlings = 'izithombo'.
'Iirekhodi zombolekisi wemali' = 'the lender's records' (possessive), not records prepared FOR a lender. Farmer could think these are the lender's own records.
Same possessive problem as R191: 'export the lender's records' instead of 'export records for a lender'.
repaired: Thumela ngaphandle iirekhodi ezenzelwe umbolekisi wemali

problem: Spelling of negative copulative: 'awububungqina' should be 'awubobungqina' (it is not proof).
repaired: Umfanekiso wesityalo owenziwe yi-AI, awubobungqina besivuno

problem: 'Ihlawulwa ngu' ('it is paid by') is a dangling preposition when shown as a label ABOVE the buyer name rather than directly joined to it. A noun label is clearer.
'Khetha kanye intengiso' reads 'choose a sale once / only one sale'; English is 'Choose the exact sale' (the correct one).
Draft says keep 'its (the invoice's) original details and any linked sale'; English says keep the original details OF any linked sale.
repaired: Le i-invoyisi ayikwazanga ukugcinwa. Jonga indawo yokugcina kwisixhobo sakho uze ugcine iinkcukacha zokuqala zentengiso nganye enxulunyanisiweyo, emva koko uzame kwakhona.

problem: 'sele ingeyenye i-invoyisi' is ambiguous: 'inge-' is the negative participial prefix, so it can read 'is already not another invoice'. English means the sale is already linked to/belongs to another invoice.
repaired: Le ntengiso sele inxulunyaniswe nenye i-invoyisi.
